app-button.summary: Styled button with variants, sizes, loading spinner, and disabled state.

variant.description: Visual style: `primary` (default, dark fill) | `secondary` (brand tint) | `tertiary` (white + hairline border; `outline` is an alias) | `ghost` | `danger` | `danger-secondary` | `ghost-danger` (red ink, no fill — the quiet destructive icon in a rail of icons) | `dark` (alias of `primary`, kept for existing call sites) | `icon`

icon-only.description: Squares the button to its size's control height with no padding, per Figma's Icon Button frame (4158:1100) — which is the same Type × Tone × Size matrix as the text button, so `variant` still supplies the colour. `variant="icon"` remains as the ghost-coloured shorthand used across mcp-page and the EE pages.

href.description: Renders an `<a class="btn">` instead of a `<button>`, so a navigation CTA is the same component as every other button. The SPA router intercepts internal anchor clicks, so no click handler is needed. A `disabled` (or `loading`) button keeps its `<button disabled>` — an anchor cannot be disabled.

loading.description: Shows a spinner and disables the button

aria-label.description: Forwarded to the inner `<button>`, which is the focusable element an AT actually names. Required on an `icon-only` button: the host is not focusable, so an aria-label left on it is never announced — and neither is a disclosure button's `aria-expanded`.

title.description: Forwarded to the inner `<button>`, which is the focusable element an AT actually names. Required on an `icon-only` button: the host is not focusable, so an aria-label left on it is never announced — and neither is a disclosure button's `aria-expanded`.

loading.description: Renders the shimmer placeholder instead of content. The skeleton lives here, not in the consuming page, so the card's geometry has exactly one definition and the loading and loaded states cannot drift apart. (The attribute below was added after the catalog first shipped and sits last on purpose: the DSL passes attributes positionally in @attr order, so a new one must append — see catalog-compat.mjs.)

error.description: *We* could not load this card's data — distinct from `status="error"`, which means the agent itself is unhealthy and the card loaded fine. Two different facts that happened to want a similar look, and only the second was expressible. Present (bare, or with a message overriding the default copy) replaces the whole card body with the shared failure block — icon, one line, Retry. `loading` wins over it.

events.name: card-retry
events.description: Retry pressed on the `error` state — bubbles. The card is handed its data, so the owner refetches.

stacked.description: `bar` only: stack datasets instead of grouping them

format.description: Value formatting: `number` (default) | `currency` | `percent` | `compact` | `tokens` | `duration` (milliseconds in, `420ms` / `1.8s` out — for a latency axis). `tokens` is an alias for `compact` and exists for one reason: AppStatCard and AppStatRow accept it, so a surface writes `format: "tokens"` on the token KPI and then, one line later, on the chart of the same numbers — and got a fatal for being consistent. Two vocabularies for one idea is our defect, not the caller's. The stat formats this still does NOT take are the ones an axis cannot mean: `bytes` (no source in scope returns any) and `date`/`time`/`datetime`/`text`, which are not magnitudes.

center-value.description: `donut` only: the figure drawn in the hole

legend.description: `auto` (default: on for donut and for 2+ series) | `on` | `off`

loading.description: Shimmer placeholder instead of the plot

label.description: Accessible name for the plot. Falls back to the type. (The four attributes below were added after the catalog first shipped and sit last on purpose: the DSL passes attributes positionally in @attr order, so a new one must append — see catalog-compat.mjs.)

segmented.description: `bar` only: the concentration presentation — every stack segment is a gapped, fully-rounded pill, the y-axis is hidden, and `stacked` is implied. Pair with `average-line` for the reference rule.

average-line.description: `bar` only: dashed horizontal rule at the mean of the column totals, labelled "avg".

format-y2.description: Right-axis formatting when a dataset declares `axis: 'y2'`: `number` (default) | `currency` | `percent` | `compact` | `tokens` | `duration`

flush-top.description: The plot's own canvas-painted background (see `plotBackground`) normally rounds all four corners, like any other surface card. Set this when another element sits directly above the chart with no gap (the day grid on the concentration panel) and the two should read as one continuous card: it squares the top two corners off, leaving only the bottom two rounded. Applies to the loading skeleton and empty state too (app-chart.css) — those are plain divs shown instead of the canvas, not something `plotBackground` paints, so they need their own override rather than inheriting this one.

error.description: The fetch failed. Present (bare, or with a message overriding the default copy) swaps the plot for the shared inline failure block — icon, one line, Retry — instead of leaving the skeleton spinning forever or, worse, showing the empty-state copy, which tells the user their data does not exist when in truth we could not ask. `loading` wins over it; it wins over empty.

The (markup) marker is what gen-catalog reads to emit `markup: true`, and gen-dsl-catalog withholds every marked attribute from the DSL vocabulary automatically. events.name: stat-card-retry
events.description: Retry pressed on the failure state — bubbles. The card is handed its value, so the owner refetches.

app-stat-row.summary: Row of headline metrics separated by hairlines — the one stat strip.

items.description: JSON array of metric objects: `{ label, value, sub, pct, format?, subFormat?, currency? }`. `sub` is the caption under the value; `pct` (a number) draws a severity meter and is omitted for metrics that have no ceiling. There is deliberately no per-metric colour: a value is a value, and the one that was tinted gold was drift, not meaning. `format` is per metric, not per strip, because a strip is precisely where a dollar figure sits next to a token count next to a latency — one attribute for all of them would be wrong for most of them. It takes the same names as `app-stat-card`'s (`currency`, `compact`, `duration`, `bytes`, `date`, …) and `currency` overrides the ISO code for that one metric. Omit it and the value is formatted by shape: a fractional number to two decimals, an ISO-8601 string as local time, a pre-built string verbatim. `sub` takes `subFormat` and the same treatment, so a caption that is just a number does not undo the work.

loading.description: Number of skeleton cells to reserve while data loads (default: 4). The skeleton lives here so it cannot drift from the real geometry. Present-but-empty means the default.

variant.description: `chips` lays the same metrics out as a wrapping row of `label: value` pills instead of hairline-separated columns — for strips that sit under a page title rather than heading a dashboard. Purely a layout change: same `items`, same cells, no second markup path. `pct` meters and `sub` captions are column-shaped and are not drawn in chips. (The attribute below was added after the catalog first shipped and sits last on purpose: the DSL passes attributes positionally in @attr order, so a new one must append — see catalog-compat.mjs.)

error.description: The fetch failed. Present (bare, or with a message overriding the default copy) replaces the whole strip with one failure block and one Retry, because one request filled every cell and one is what failed. Without it a failed strip printed a dash per metric — the same dash an honest zero prints, so "we could not get this" and "this is nothing" were indistinguishable. `loading` wins over it.

events.name: stat-row-retry
events.description: Retry pressed on the failure state — bubbles. The strip is handed its metrics, so the owner refetches.

app-switch.summary: On/off toggle with an optional label and subtext.

layout.description: `inline` (default, control then label) | `settings` (label left, control pushed to the far right — Figma Layout=Settings, for settings rows).

name.description: Forwarded to the inner `<input type="checkbox">`. Pass `aria-label` when there is no visible `label`.

value.description: Forwarded to the inner `<input type="checkbox">`. Pass `aria-label` when there is no visible `label`.

aria-label.description: Forwarded to the inner `<input type="checkbox">`. Pass `aria-label` when there is no visible `label`.

events.name: change
events.description: Bubbles from the inner input.

app-table.summary: Paginated data table — search, sortable auto-detected columns, an optional row-detail panel, and numbered page navigation.

limit.description: Rows per page (default: 10). Ignored for `pagination="none"`, which renders whatever the data function returns.

pagination.description: `pages` (default) — prev / windowed page numbers / next — or `none` for no pager at all. Optional: omit it and you get pages.

data-fn.description: Name of a registered data source (see core/data-sources.js), called as `(query, page, limit)` and returning `{ data, total }` or a bare array. `page` is 1-based. Alternatively assign the `dataFn` property directly and call `refresh()` yourself.

detail.description: Present: clicking a row opens a detail modal. A boolean, not a string: `#showDetail` is `hasAttribute('detail')` and the value is never read. It was typed `{string}` here, which made it a string in the catalog, which made `detail="false"` *enable* the modal — and a generated surface writing `false` into that position (which it does, to reach `empty-message` after it) therefore turned on a row-click modal nobody asked for, on every table, silently.

empty-message.description: Body text when there are no rows and no query.

loading.description: Hold the skeleton: the owner has not got rows yet and will hand them over later. Present suppresses the fetch entirely, so a table waiting on data upstream never flashes its empty state first; removing it fetches. Every other data component in the design system has this, and a caller who reasonably assumed this one did too was writing an argument that landed in the next slot along.

error.description: The fetch failed. Present (bare, or with a message overriding the default copy) draws the shared failure block in the table body — icon, one line, Retry — under a live header row, in place of the rows. Set automatically when this table's own `dataFn` throws; settable by an owner that feeds the table itself. `loading` wins over it.

events.name: loading-start
events.description: Before each fetch — bubbles.

events.name: loading-end
events.description: After each fetch — bubbles.

events.name: table-retry
events.description: Retry pressed on the failure state — bubbles. The table also refetches through its own `dataFn` first, where it has one; the event is for an owner that supplies rows itself.

app-tabs.summary: Tab bar in two shapes: - **Panels** (default) — `[data-tab]` (or `[data-slot]`) children are the panels; the strip is generated from their `data-label` — or from the `tabs` attribute, which is how a generated surface names them — and the component owns which one shows.

tabs.description: JSON array of `{ key, label }` naming the panels (panels mode). Each key matches a child's `data-tab` or `data-slot`. Optional: without it the strip reads each panel's `data-label`, falling back to the key.

active.description: Key of the active tab (panels mode). Reflected as the user switches.

query-param.description: URL param kept in sync with the active tab (panels mode)

label.description: Accessible name of the tablist, e.g. `Agent sections`.

data-tab.description: The panel's key; matches a `tabs` entry. `data-slot` is the same thing.

data-label.description: Strip label for the panel when `tabs` does not name it.

events.name: tabs-change
events.description: Tab switched; `detail: { key: string }` — bubbles

app-tag.summary: Tag / chip — an interactive, content-bearing label.

selected.description: Gold fill. The filter chip's on state.

image.description: src for the circular leading image (provider logo, avatar).

events.name: tag-change
events.description: `{ selected }` after a `selectable` tag toggles.

events.name: tag-remove
events.description: Cancelable; the tag removes itself unless prevented.

app-tag-group.summary: A row of `<app-tag>`s that behaves as one filter control.

selection.description: `multiple` (default) | `single` | `none` — `none` is a plain layout row with no selection behaviour (the Flutter default).

value.description: Selected tag values, space-separated. Reflected as the user picks. Each tag's value is its `value` attribute, falling back to its text.

scrollable.description: One line, horizontal scroll, instead of wrapping.

excludedFromCatalog.reason: deprecated alias of selection; removed next release

events.name: tag-group-change
events.description: `{ value: string[] }` after a selection change.

app-text.summary: Typography — a heading, a paragraph, a caption, an eyebrow label.

app-textarea.summary: Multi-line text input with the same label / hint / count / state contract as `<app-input>`.

hint.description: Helper line below the box. Turns red in `state="error"`.

count.description: Right-aligned counter in the hint row, e.g. `120/500`. With `maxlength` set and no `count`, the counter is derived live.

max-rows.description: Growth ceiling; beyond it the box scrolls. Omit for no ceiling.

resizable.description: Shows the native corner grip. Off by default — auto-grow covers the common case and a grip fights it.

value.description: Forwarded to the inner `<textarea>`.

events.name: input
events.description: Bubbles from the inner textarea.

events.name: change
events.description: Bubbles from the inner textarea.

app-time-field.summary: Inline time editor: `HH : MM` segments, optional seconds, optional AM/PM.

value.description: `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS`, 24-hour. Reflected on change.

min.description: Earliest time, `HH:MM[:SS]`. A complete value below it snaps up.

name.description: Forwarded to a hidden native input for form submit.

excludedFromCatalog.reason: deprecated alias of format; removed next release

events.name: change
events.description: `{ value }` when the segments form a complete time. Bubbles.

app-toggle.summary: Two-state (pressed / unpressed) button — "Bold" in a formatting toolbar.

pressed.description: The on state. Reflected as the user toggles.

value.description: Identifier echoed by `<app-toggle-group>` in its events.

aria-label.description: Forwarded to the inner button. Required when icon-only.

events.name: toggle-change
events.description: `{ pressed, value }` after a user toggle. Bubbles.

app-toggle-group.summary: A row of `<app-toggle>`s with single or multiple selection.

value.description: In `single` mode, the `value` of the pressed item. Reflected as the user picks. In `multiple` mode, a space-separated list.

attached.description: Fuses the items into one segmented bar (shared hairlines, radius on the outer corners only). CSS-only.

excludedFromCatalog.reason: deprecated alias of selection; removed next release

events.name: toggle-group-change
events.description: `{ value }` — a string in `single` mode, an array in `multiple`.

app-toolbar.summary: Horizontal toolbar with named start and end slots for grouping actions.

aria-label.description: Accessible label for the toolbar region

app-trace-tree.summary: Tree of timed spans: a nested run where every node carries a duration and an outcome — a distributed trace, a call graph, a build's step tree.

spans.description: JSON array of root nodes, each `{ id, label, meta?, icon?, status?, duration?, children? }`: `id` is echoed in both events, `meta` is the mono line beside the label (an operation name), `icon` names a glyph from the shared set, `status` is `ok` (default) or `error`, `duration` is the formatted time on the trailing badge.

value.description: `id` of the selected row.

collapsed.description: JSON array of node ids whose children are hidden.

events.name: trace-tree-select
events.description: `{ id }` when a row is clicked or activated.

events.name: trace-tree-toggle
events.description: `{ id, expanded }` from the disclosure chevron.
